clues: This city stands by a great river where the green delta fans out to the sea. Stone pyramids built by kings of old rise at its edge.
This desert city sees rain so rarely that it falls only in the cool months. Yet one sudden shower can flood the streets in a rush.
New rulers built this city from scratch in the year 969 as their royal seat. Four years later it was the proud capital of their wide realm.
A famed bazaar in the old town here has drawn traders since the days of the Mamluks, hundreds of years past. Craft workers still make fine goods in its busy lanes.
Egypt's rulers govern the land from this city, its capital and largest town. The Arab League keeps its head office here too, by the great river.
